correctness.rationale: An incidence-tree geodesic is unique and its internal original vertices are precisely relevant articulation vertices. The rooted subtree states partition internally valid nonempty sets by compatibility with any selected outside vertex, yielding the displayed recurrences by exhaustive separation into no B-child, single B-child, and selected-root cases. The operation count is charged to subtree sizes/pairs at their lowest common ancestor. Actual embedded Python verifier checked 3,000 small graphs and 2,068,500 subsets against independent breadth-first-search triple tests, plus larger blocks; finite tests supplement the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2018 block-graph theorem gives only the extremal size, while the 2024 general-position polynomial paper gives generic inclusion-exclusion and special families, not a general block-cut-tree recurrence or a quadratic coefficient algorithm. Published special-family formulas for caterpillars, spiders and windmills do not dominate the unrestricted theorem. Targeted research-record and scholarly-source searches found no equivalent result; residual risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named enumeration algorithms, including possible earlier block-graph betweenness-polynomial formulations, may exist.
The mobile-position paper was compared by its abstract and invariant distinction, not a complete text; it is not a decisive unresolved coverage source.

value.rationale: The full cardinality distribution on arbitrary connected block graphs is a natural and strictly richer object than known maximum-cardinality results. The \(O(n^2)\) coefficient algorithm handles arbitrary trees of cliques, including all trees and unrestricted articulation patterns, without exponential maximal-set enumeration. This is a substantive structural uniform algorithm, not an arbitrary finite slice or routine special case.
